# How to generate AI images in Picsart: a beginner's step-by-step guide

> **In short:** Picsart has a built-in AI image generator that turns your text prompts into pictures, then lets you keep editing in the same conversation. The AI tools usually sit behind a paid plan, and the engine works best with still images — not video.

If you've ever opened Picsart to fix a photo, design a poster, or make a quick thumbnail, the app already has an AI image generator tucked inside. Type a sentence, and Picsart turns it into a picture. Don't like something in the result? Stay in the same chat and ask for a change — the AI keeps the rest of the image intact. Here's how to try it, step by step, even if you've never touched an AI image tool before.

## Before you start
- A Picsart account — sign-up is free, but AI image generation usually requires a paid plan. Check Picsart's current pricing page before you start.
- The Picsart app on your phone or tablet, or the web version in your browser at picsart.com.
- A rough idea of what you want to make: a poster, a product mock-up, a photo edit, or a wallpaper.
- About 10 minutes for your first image.

## Step 1 — Open Picsart and find the AI image generator
Open the Picsart app and sign in. Once you're on the home screen, look for a tile, button, or section whose name suggests AI image generation — common labels include **AI Image Generator**, **AI Playground**, or **Text to Image**. If you don't see any of those on the main grid, tap the **+** (plus) button at the bottom-center of the screen, or look for a **Create** tab along the bottom row of icons — the AI tools usually live in one of those two places. On the web version at picsart.com, look in the top menu for something like **AI Tools** or **Create**.

💬 Example: this step has nothing to type — just finding the right entry point.

You'll know it worked when a screen appears with a text field where you can describe the image you want (usually called the prompt box) and at least one option to either start from text or upload a photo.

## Step 2 — Pick your starting point: text, photo, or template
Inside the AI image tool, you'll usually see a few big choices near the top of the screen: **Text to Image** (start from a written description), **Image to Image** (start from a photo you upload), or a ready-made template you can fill in. Tap whichever fits what you want — for your first try, choose **Text to Image** if it's available. If the screen also shows a model selector — a small dropdown, a chip near the prompt box, or a tile in a side panel — pick whichever option is marked as the latest or recommended. Picsart rotates AI models over time, and the list changes often, so we won't name a specific one here.

💬 Example: this step is a tap, not a typing step — the key choice is **Text to Image** for a first run.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows an empty prompt box and a clearly labeled button like **Generate**, **Create**, or an arrow icon.

## Step 3 — Choose a canvas size (if the app asks)
Before you write your prompt, some versions of the tool show a size or shape picker. If you see it — usually a small icon shaped like a square, a rectangle, or a phone outline, or a dropdown near the prompt box — pick the shape that matches where you'll use the picture. A square shape works for Instagram-style posts, a tall rectangle works for phone wallpapers and Stories, and a wide rectangle works for banners and YouTube thumbnails. If the app also shows a quality choice (sometimes labeled with letters or numbers like 1K, 2K, or 4K, where higher means sharper but slower), pick the lowest one for a quick test so you don't burn through your credits.

💬 Example: for a square post, choose the square option; for a phone wallpaper, choose the tall rectangle; if you see a quality choice, pick the lowest setting for a quick test.

You'll know it worked when a small preview, a number, or a labeled chip on the screen shows the shape and size you picked.

## Step 4 — Write your prompt and generate the image
In the prompt box, describe the picture you want in plain, specific language. Name the subject, the mood, the colors, the lighting, and any text you want visible on the image — Picsart says its AI image generator handles on-image text reasonably well, which is useful for posters and diagrams. The more concrete you are, the closer the result will be to what you imagined. Then tap the **Generate** button (sometimes labeled **Create** or shown as an arrow icon). After a few seconds, one or more images appear on screen — pick the one you like best, or tap **Regenerate** if none feel right.

💬 Example: "A friendly poster for a Saturday morning yoga class, soft pastel colors, with the words 'Saturday Morning Yoga' clearly readable in the center, hand-drawn style."

You'll know it worked when a finished image appears on screen and matches the canvas shape you picked in Step 3.

## Step 5 — Refine the image in the same chat
Here's where the in-chat editing saves time: you don't have to start over when something's off. Stay in the same conversation and send a follow-up message describing one specific change. The AI keeps the rest of the picture intact and adjusts only what you asked for. You can chain several refinements one after another — change colors, swap a background, add a logo, rewrite the on-image text — without losing the previous version. Be specific: name the exact color, the exact word, the exact object. If you can't find the chat box, look for a field at the bottom of the screen that says something like **Message**, **Ask anything**, or **Describe a change**.

💬 Example: after the yoga poster above, send: "Make the background soft pink, change the words to 'Bring a friend!', and add a small sun in the top-right corner."

You'll know it worked when the new image shows your specific change and the rest of the picture still looks like the previous version.

## Step 6 — Edit an existing photo (optional)
If you'd rather start from a picture you already have, look for an **Upload** or **Image** button near the prompt box — usually shown as a small picture icon or a + sign. Tap it and pick a photo from your device. Once the photo appears, describe the edit you want in the prompt box. For finer control, look for a brush or markup tool near the image — common labels are **Mask**, **Edit**, or a small paint-bucket or brush icon. With that tool, drag your finger across the part of the photo you want changed; the painted area is the only part the AI will redraw. Then write a short note in the prompt box describing what should appear there. Be specific about what to remove, replace, or add.

💬 Example: upload a group photo, then type: "Remove the person in the red shirt on the right." Or paint over the background with the brush tool and write: "Replace this background with a sunset beach."

You'll know it worked when the edited photo appears with your specific change applied and the rest of the image still looks natural.

## Step 7 — Save and export your image
When you're happy with the result, look for a **Save**, **Download**, or **Export** button — usually at the top-right corner of the image or inside a **⋯** (three dots) menu. The app may ask you to pick a file format: choose **JPG** for everyday sharing, or **PNG** if you need a transparent background (for layering the image on top of other designs). The image then saves to your device's photo gallery or your computer's Downloads folder. If you want to keep editing the file inside Picsart later, look for a **Save to project** or **Save as draft** option instead.

💬 Example: not a typing step — the key choice is **JPG** for everyday sharing, **PNG** only if you need a transparent background.

You'll know it worked when the image file appears in your phone's gallery (or your computer's Downloads folder) and opens like any normal picture.

## Common mistakes
- **Picking the wrong starting mode.** If you upload a photo but meant to start from text (or the other way around), the result will look off. In Step 2, double-check you've chosen the right mode — **Text to Image** or **Image to Image** — before tapping Generate.
- **Asking for vague edits.** "Make it better" or "fix it" gives the AI nothing to act on. Always name the specific change: a color, an object, a word, a mood. The more concrete the instruction, the closer the result.
- **Forgetting the cost.** Each generation usually spends credits or counts against your plan's allowance. A higher-quality image costs more than a lower-quality one, and each follow-up edit in the chat counts as another generation. Check your remaining credits before kicking off a long chain of edits — otherwise the tool may stop mid-conversation.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can make a custom birthday card, a flyer for a school bake sale, or a fun wallpaper for your phone — in minutes, without any design training.
- **For your business or work:** You can mock up a quick social-media post, an event poster, or a product visual to share with a colleague before commissioning a designer for the final version.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one simple text-to-image prompt (Step 4) at the lowest quality setting. Get a feel for what the tool does well before moving on to photo edits or higher-quality output.

## Try it now
Open Picsart, find the AI image generator, and create one square image of your favorite season — one sentence prompt, no edits, just see what comes back. Takes about two minutes.
